findings.finding: N2 ('surface stays comfortable, doesn't turn sticky/smell') and N4 ('need to know before I buy whether it fits my desk's edge shape') are both labeled pain_level 'latent' — defined as hidden, barely felt, buyer not looking. But this same buyer explicitly names both worries, unprompted, as ranked fears (fear rank 2 and rank 4) before seeing any diagram or bullet, and N4 is directly tied to fears the buyer says they'd otherwise 'guess and risk a return' on. A buyer actively articulating and ranking a worry is not exhibiting latent pain by the framework's own definition — that's moderate pain, like N1 and N3 (correctly labeled 'moderate'). Unresolved across two passes; left open by design since it belongs to buyer, not innovaty, and the fix loop was scoped to innovaty's two high findings.
findings.fix: Re-rate N2 and N4 as pain_level 'moderate' (or justify in evidence why an explicitly self-articulated, ranked fear is still latent), and re-check whether innovaty's spend allocation, which weights by pain depth, under-prioritized these needs on the mistaken assumption they were only latent.

findings.finding: The pre-clone win probability of 0.55 treats a brand-new, zero-review listing as a near-coin-flip winner against VAYDEER's 2,045-review, 4.6-star incumbent on day one. This is not reconciled with the review-gating logic genius's own forecast otherwise respects (moore.chasm, gate.social_proof, months 1-3 modeled as innovator-only 1-5% share) or with buyer's three_second_scan, where social proof is exactly what pulls the click toward VAYDEER, not an unknown new entrant. Unresolved across two passes; carried forward as a watch item since it did not block readiness and the fix loop was scoped to innovaty's two high findings.
findings.fix: Either lower win_probability_before_clones to reflect the review-chasm the listing starts inside of, or add an explicit reason (e.g. 'conditioned on accumulating ~50+ reviews before the clone wave lands') so the number doesn't silently assume the review gap has already closed.

findings.finding: States 'I1's design registration, I5's spec badge and I2's fit diagram are the plan's actual moat' as if the three carry comparable weight. But competition itself rates I2's packaging_experience moat 'weak' and says explicitly a cloner 'won't bother replicating it in their first wave' — a temporary, first-wave-only deterrent, not durable protection like design_registration (medium, legally actionable). Folding a weak, soon-clonable item into the same breath as the strongest moat overstates the plan's actual defensibility to the founder. Unresolved across two passes; carried forward as a watch item.
findings.fix: Qualify the founder summary to distinguish the durable moat (design registration) from the soft, temporary ones (spec badge, fit diagram), and note the packaging/spec items only buy time in the first clone wave, not lasting protection.

findings.finding: Claims the walnut-wood background will make the product 'visibly pop against the four look-alike tiles on the page,' implying all four page-one competitors share a similar (dark) background. Scout only confirmed a background description for VAYDEER ('dark desk'); Jelbows, Leolee and Fuzadel's main_image_description fields give no background color at all. Unresolved across two passes; low severity, carried forward as a watch item.
findings.fix: Either scope the claim to what's actually confirmed ('differentiates from VAYDEER's dark-desk anchor, the only background scout could confirm') or have scout capture the other three listings' actual background/thumbnail treatment before asserting grid-wide differentiation.

findings.finding: States 'I6's magnet-adjacent concerns from the knowledge base do not apply — this product carries no magnet.' No idea in this run (I1-I6) involves a magnet in any form; I6 is a pure geometry/symmetry change, not a magnet mechanism. This reads as a boilerplate knowledge-base line pattern-matched onto an unrelated idea. Unresolved across two passes; low severity, carried forward as a watch item.
findings.fix: Drop the false I6/magnet reference and simply state the product contains no magnetic components, confirmed against the actual BOM (foam, fabric, rubber, printed card, woven tag).

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: Two fix loops resolved everything high-severity: the durability review now names a real dimensional change (bond-keying depth increased to a minimum 2.5mm, plus a new witness-line indicator), the main hero image now correctly shows v1's actual asymmetric shape instead of a deferred, unfunded ambidextrous geometry, and the ERRC list no longer claims that deferred feature is already shipping. The witness-line detail has also now been priced into the BOM (a small pad-print/ink-marking step, not new tooling) and added to I3's proving test.

Two open items still deserve a look before you fund this: the day-one 55% win-probability-before-clones number assumes near-equal footing against VAYDEER's 2,045-review lead with zero reviews of your own — that contradicts the review-gated ramp (innovator-only volume, months 1-3) the rest of the plan itself uses, so expect a slower early climb, especially with a clone wave arriving in 1-4 months per competition's own numbers. And the founder summary lumps a weak, easily-cloned moat (the fit-diagram insert) in with the durable one (design registration) — treat the registered profile as your real protection, the rest as a first-wave head start only.

Two buyer needs (surface staying non-tacky, and knowing before purchase whether it fits your desk edge) are self-articulated ranked fears but are still labeled 'latent' pain rather than 'moderate' — worth a second look since spend allocation weights by pain depth, and these may be under-funded relative to how much buyers actually care.
